calls.reasoning: Resolves as (UI forecaster count on the close date) / (days open), tenth-rounded. The numerator is directly observed and undisputed across all three runs: 119 (Sep 11) -> 128 -> 135 -> 144 -> 153 (live, 2026-09-20), a flat 4.2/day with no decay, projecting to ~188 over the 8.22 days to the Sep 28 05:59Z close, with a late-entrant bump from the Fall season opening the instant this closes and saturation near the ~173-bot roster pulling the other way; 153 is a hard floor. All uncertainty is in the denominator, which is unpublished (API 403, no opened/published string on the page, no Wayback snapshot). Two independent lines bound it: post IDs are monotone at creation and twin post 45517 shows 'Closes Sep 5, 2028', putting creation at ~Sep 5, while third-party tournament metadata and the 'published before the tournament start date' issue put the open before ~Sep 10 - so D is 19-23 days. Within that, nine days of zero decay fits days 6-15 of a Sep 5 open better than days 2-11 of a Sep 9 open, which kills Sep 8-9 but not Sep 7, the Monday on which the ID-adjacent MiniBench block 45518-45577 opened. 188/23=8.2, 188/21=9.0; the mixture medians at 8.5. The on-page bot-only aggregate (~5.4) implies D>=34 at any numerator compatible with 153 and the same mechanism misprices the twin ~8x - not blended. No market exists on this quantity.
calls.reconciliation: In dispute: (a) whether the '14 forecasters on Sep 9' trace belongs to this post or to identically-titled twin 45517 - FACTUAL, and decisive, since 14 on Sep 9 would force an open near Sep 8-9 and a quotient near 9.9. Settled for the twin: Runs 1 and 3 independently report 45517's own series as 14/27/35/39/45 on Sep 9/11/15/17/20 while both report 45516 starting at 119 on Sep 11, so two independent runs place that exact value on the twin. (b) The scaffold's first-touch on Sep 9 as an open-date signal - FACTUAL, de-weighted: Run 2 shows the scaffold was still polling the Summer feed on Sep 6 (forecasting Summer ids 44651-44695), so first-touch dates the slug switchover, not the open. (c) Whether the ~5.4 on-page aggregate deserves weight - FACTUAL by arithmetic, and it does not: it requires D>=34, which the creation bound excludes. (d) The open date itself - JUDGMENT, and unsettleable from the dossiers: no run retrieved open_time and no anonymous surface carries it. I could not break this tie with evidence, so I let it carry its real spread rather than collapsing it. Where I depart from all three runs: each placed its median at D~22.5 (a Sep 5-6 open) while Run 2's own text concedes Sep 6-9 'stays live at ~48%'. The decay-shape argument they use to justify the early open discriminates against Sep 8-9, not against Sep 7 - and Sep 7 is the Monday the ID-adjacent block opened, which is the single most specific open-date anchor anyone found. Giving Sep 7 the weight their own ID reasoning implies moves the median to 8.5, modestly above all three. Numerator, escape logic, market check (none found) and the aggregate dismissal are carried forward unchanged; I retrieved nothing myself this run, so 'sources' is empty by design.
